thread:
jamie: incident-bot reports repeated OOMs on serving-rt pods in us-east1-a, started ~16:14 UTC. container restarts + CUDA errors in the logs. low traffic but noisy failures. @alex can you grab logs?

oncall-bot: [ALERT] node-12b serving-rt: frequent restarts (5x in 6m) — severity: P2 — incident_id: INC-2026-459

alex: looking. docker logs show repeated: 
```
# tail -n 60 /var/log/pods/serving-rt/serving-rt-xyz.log
E 16:12:41 runtime: cudaMemcpyAsync failed: out of memory
W 16:12:41 allocator: attn-pool allocation failed for 128MB page (try=3)
I 16:12:41 kv-cache: page split triggered, free_pages=2
E 16:12:42 containerd: starting restart loop: exit code 137
```

alex: also seeing kernel OOM kill entries for process redwood-serve. seems memory creeping until total GPU mem exhausted and driver triggers process kill.

nina: ok this smells like slow leak in attention allocator + fragmented KV cache. previous incidents had similar pattern but this one is on a single node flaring. low RPS so likely per-worker leak rather than overall load.

jamie: mitigation steps I'm about to run: 1) cordon + drain node-12b (move pods to other AZs), 2) scale down runtime replicas for affected nodepool to reduce concurrent KV warmups, 3) route traffic away from model variant 'redwood-large-v2' in us-east1-a to fallback 'redwood-medium' for 10m window, 4) start a kv-compact job on other healthy nodes to force evictions.

jamie: running drain now: `kubectl drain node-12b --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force` :hammer:

oncall-bot: node-12b cordoned by jamie at 16:18 UTC.

elaine: started the fallback routing config in traffic-router. pushing 100% of us-east1-a traffic to us-east1-b/c for redwood-large-v2. will keep telemetry up.

alex: node drain succeeded, but two pods failed to come up in other AZs due to slow page warmup; logs show a repeated 'attn-pool: page map fragmentation, cannot fulfill contiguous allocation' warning. linking sample trace: 
```
E 16:19:04 attn-pool: fragmented slab (free_chunks=18, max_contig=12) request=32
E 16:19:05 allocator: tried fallback paged-alloc path, slow path latency=120ms
```

nina: this suggests a KV page fragmentation pattern where freed pages are scattered causing contiguous page requests to fail and trigger gradual growth of allocations until OOM. Need to force compaction and reduce contiguous allocation sizes in the hot path.

jamie: customer impact: ~2% of serving requests in the last 30m returned 503s or were retried. one Dedicated customer (acct: ACCT-998) reported degraded latency ~16:10 UTC; support ticket #SUP-6123 opened. Not a widespread outage but unacceptable for dedicated SLAs.

alex: I've captured a heap snapshot and CUDA driver logs; uploading to /tmp/triage/4051236789/ . grep points to repeated allocation patterns from attention kernel when sequence_len > 4096 and kv cache warmup triggers.

nina: immediate live mitigations (short list):
- reduce max_concurrency for runtime in affected pool to 1
- decrease default batching window to 25ms
- disable prefetch for kv cache on canary nodes
- trigger `kv-compact --aggressive` on all hosts in pool (rolling, low-IO)

jamie: implemented max_concurrency reduction and batch window change. applied `runtime.config.max_concurrency=1` via rollout to pool-12.

oncall-bot: runtime pool-12 config updated by jamie at 16:29 UTC.

elaine: kv-compact job submitted (job id kvc-4051). it's running on 3 nodes, low IO. progress logs show compaction freeing ~1.2GB across nodes after first pass.

alex: after compaction, we're seeing fewer allocation failures. however one node (node-9c) still shows occasional container restart with exit 137 ~ every 15m. suspect residual fragmentation + per-process leak.

nina: plan for next 2 hours:
1) schedule hotfix rollout of runtime 1.4.2 which includes attention allocator guardrails (limits contiguous page request and backfills smaller chunks).
2) run kv-compact globally during low traffic window in 30m.
3) run memory-leak-detect instrumentation on canary to gather tech traces (heap + cuda mem maps)
4) reach out to Dedicated customer ops to inform about mitigation and ETA.

jamie: pinging @ops for possible maintenance window if hotfix requires short restarts. ops: telemetry shows low traffic at ~00:30 UTC, may be ideal for global compaction.

elaine: messaging to customers drafted:
"We observed a localized memory fragmentation issue in our serving runtime that caused increased restarts on a small set of nodes and degraded latency for a subset of requests. We've routed traffic away from impacted nodes, applied concurrency and batching limits, and are rolling a runtime patch. We're monitoring and will follow up with a detailed RCA." :eyes:

oncall-bot: CREATED INCIDENT-2026-459-EXTRA with summary "serving runtime memory fragmentation -> node restart flapping". severity remains P2.

nina: I'm taking this incident for the next hour. jamie — leaving notes in the channel about commands run and paths to logs. handoff: please escalate to infra if compaction job triggers storage pressure.

jamie: acknowledged. logs+artifacts: /tmp/triage/4051236789/ (heap snapshots, cuda logs, kv-compact output).

alex: adding command snippets for followup: 
```
# force a compact on a host
ssh node-9c sudo /usr/local/bin/kv-compact --aggressive --max-io=50
# runtime agent restart (graceful)
kubectl rollout restart daemonset/runtime-agent -n redwood-serving
```

nina: leaving oncall note: probable root vectors = combination of attention allocator contiguous-request regression + slow kv cache fragmentation + large sequence workloads causing contiguous allocations. mitigation = runtime guardrails + aggressive compaction + routing fallbacks.

jamie: thanks team. nina, take over and ping when you need escalation. I'll sync with support on SUP-6123. :thumbsup:

nina: taking over now. will update incident timeline and keep channel posted.

elaine: keeping traffic routing on fallback for 20m then reevaluate.

oncall-bot: last update 16:34 UTC — incident assigned to nina.

jamie: P.S. file a follow-up task for adding an automated compaction trigger when fragmentation metrics exceed threshold (metric: attn_pool.max_contig / attn_pool.free_chunks)."
